correctness.rationale: The Dyck-vector hull equals the explicit coordinate/ballot-prefix halfspace system: after cumulative-sum coordinates its constraints form a totally unimodular network matrix. Intrinsic coordinate normals have squared norm (m-1)/m, while a prefix of length 2k has squared normal norm 2k(m-2k)/m. The first two-coordinate cap and first prefix force the upper bound r<=1/[2(a_m+c_m)]; the opposite-half sign construction satisfies every inward-shifted inequality because sqrt((m-t)/(mt)) is maximal at t=2. The two endpoint prefix constraints force first and last coordinate pairs at equality for every incenter; middle coordinates with one sum constraint admit a relative-interior point for n>=4, proving dimension 2n-7. Small cases n=2,3, strict monotonicity and the limit are handled separately. Numeric LP tests across n=3..34 and exact Dyck enumerations n=3..8 passed; these corroborate, do not establish, the proof.

originality.rationale: The 2012 primary facet description and 2017 Ehrhart/distributive results supply the underlying halfspace model but do not state the metric theorem. The present argument gives a sharp inradius 1/[2(a_m+c_m)], matching all-dimensional lower/upper bounds and a codimension-four incenter locus; neither follows merely from the published Ehrhart or valuative formulas. Search comparisons of exact statement, synonyms and stronger coverage revealed no matching result, with residual historical-priority risk acknowledged.

value.rationale: The Catalan matroid is canonical, and intrinsic inradius/incenter freedom are natural Euclidean invariants not encoded by its Catalan vertex count or Ehrhart polynomial. The finding gives the exact all-rank invariant, a nonzero asymptotic radius in growing dimension, and a striking codimension-four family of maximum-ball centers. The explicit center inequalities permit geometric comparisons and future optimization in the same metric. It is a complete, motivated geometric classification rather than an arbitrary finite computation or small numerical improvement.
